messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: I would like information on money market accounts.\nassistant: A money market account is a type of bank account that combines features of traditional checking and savings accounts. It is insured in the same way as other deposits and offers check-writing and electronic transfer functionalities. Money market accounts were introduced due to the high inflation of the 1970s, allowing banks to fund each other's loans through asset-backed securities held in these accounts. They typically pay a higher interest rate than checking accounts but have restrictions on withdrawal frequency. Money market accounts are suitable for parking some of your emergency fund due to their liquidity and ease of access. It is essential to distinguish between money market funds (mutual funds) and money market accounts (bank accounts). Money market funds may pay dividends, and you would receive a 1099-DIV, while money market accounts pay interest and you would receive a 1099-INT. If a broker set up the account and your statements mention FDIC coverage, it is likely a bank account and will pay interest, not dividends. There are some disadvantages to saving money in a money market account as your money is readily available. However, it can still be a good option for a portion of your emergency fund precisely due to its liquidity and easy access.\nuser: Which pays better interest, a savings or money market account? \nassistant: A money market account generally pays a higher interest rate than a savings account because of its structure, The actual rates offered can vary depending on the bank or financial institution, and online banks may offer better rates than traditional banks. It is always a good idea to compare rates from different providers to ensure you are getting the best deal possible. Keep in mind that money market accounts may have restrictions on withdrawal frequency, while savings accounts typically allow for unlimited withdrawals, although they are subject to federal transaction limits. Money market accounts are currently a far better choice than traditional checking accounts but pay less than savings accounts. \nuser: What are federal transaction limits?\nassistant: Federal transaction limits refer to the regulations set by the Federal Reserve that limit the number of certain types of transactions that can be made from savings accounts per month. These limits are designed to encourage savings behavior by limiting the ease of access to funds in savings accounts compared to checking accounts. As of now, savings accounts are typically limited to six withdrawals or transfers per statement cycle, including online and mobile transfers, automatic transfers, overdraft protection transfers, and telephone transfers. Exceeding these limits may result in penalties or the conversion of the savings account to a checking account. However, you should be aware that not all withdrawal types fall under this \"6 transaction\" limit. The regulations talk about \"convenient transactions,\" which generally include things like automated payments, debit card, check, internet transfers, etc. Cash withdrawals in person or at an ATM generally do not fall under this limit, so that is an option for you if you hit your limit for the month.  Money market accounts also have similar federal transaction limits.\nuser: I read that money market accounts bank accounts carry some risk versus a checking or savings account. Is that true and, if so, what kind of risk?\nassistant: It is true that money market accounts can carry some risks, but it is essential to understand that these risks are generally low compared to other investment options. One risk associated with money market accounts is the possibility of losing value due to inflation. While money market accounts typically offer higher interest rates than checking or savings accounts, the rate may not keep up with inflation, resulting in a decrease in purchasing power over time.\nAnother risk to consider is the potential for the bank or financial institution offering the money market account to fail. However, money market accounts are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, which significantly reduces this risk.\nLastly, some money market accounts may invest in short-term debt securities, such as commercial paper or Treasury bills. While these investments are generally considered low risk, there is still a chance that the issuer could default on their obligations, leading to a loss of principal.\nOverall, while money market accounts do carry some risks, they are relatively low compared to other investment options. It is crucial to understand these risks and weigh them against the potential benefits before deciding to open a money market account.\nuser: I know someone who had customer service issues with an online bank. How safe are they compared to brick-and-mortar banks.\nassistant: Online banks usually offer better rates than traditional banks and can be just as safe as brick-and-mortar banks, as long as they are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) or the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) for credit unions. These institutions provide insurance coverage for up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, protecting customers' funds in the event of a bank failure. However, it is essential to note that customer service experiences can vary between online and brick-and-mortar banks. Online banks may have limitations in personalized service or face-to-face interaction, which could lead to dissatisfaction. If your friend had a negative experience with a specific online bank, it does not necessarily mean that all online banks are unsafe or have poor customer service. Look for people who have done business with online banks. If you don't know anyone who has used their services, look for a company that at least has a brick and mortar branch in your area. Being able to deal with them face to face is a good idea. You might try checking with your local bank. It is always a good idea to research and compare different banks based on factors such as interest rates, fees, and customer reviews before making a decision. \nuser: I don't feel safe using online banking. You always hear news stories about hackers and security breaches.",
    "answer": "The provided documents do not establish how safe online banking is generally or compare it with branch-based banking. They do clearly advise never giving your online banking username or password to anyone—including someone claiming to represent your bank—because such a request may be a scam. [S1]"
}

The provided documents do not compare the safety of online banking with the safety of branch-based banking.
The provided documents clearly advise against sharing online banking usernames or passwords with any person. [S1]
The advice against sharing online banking usernames or passwords also applies to people claiming to represent a bank. [S1]
